results.title: Neuroanatomy
results.question: What brain regions does the antennal lobe connect to?
results.response: The [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") is connected to various brain regions, including the mushroom body and lateral horn, through tracts and nerves. results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response: The LPLC2 visual neuron type is known to be a lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron with a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer. It is located in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind and has its main dendritic arbors in layers 4 and 5B of the lobula, with minor processes in layer 5A, and presynaptic sites in layer 4. The LPLC2 visual neuron type projects to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP, anterior to LPLC1 and dorsal to LC4. Its activity elicits a jump escape response. VFB holds information about the LPLC2 visual neuron type, including its dendritic arbor arrangement, which allows it to detect looming stimuli, and its cholinergic nature. According to the information available from VFB, the LPLC2 visual neuron type has approximately 80 cells per optic lobe. The connectivity of the LPLC2 visual neuron type involves presynaptic sites in layer 4 of the lobula and a projection to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP.

results.title: Shared connectivity
results.question: Do the alpha/beta and gamma Kenyon cells converge on any of the same downstream MBON types? Which MBONs receive input from both?
results.response: The connectome data indicates that alpha/beta Kenyon cells and gamma Kenyon cells converge on the same downstream [mushroom body output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047953 "Open mushroom body output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") types. VFB records show that some mushroom body output neurons receive input from both alpha/beta Kenyon cells and gamma Kenyon cells. Specifically, VFB found 13 shared downstream target classes among the compared source classes, including mushroom body output neuron 32 and mushroom body output neuron 29. VFB holds extensive data on the connectivity of mushroom body output neurons, including [2788](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for MBON") downstream connectivity classes and [2077](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for MBON") upstream connectivity classes. results.title: Cross-region connectivity
results.question: What neuron types connect the central complex to the lateral accessory lobe, and how strong are these connections?

The neuron types that connect the [adult central complex](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003632 "Open adult central complex in Virtual Fly Brain") to the [lateral accessory lobe on L3 CNS template, Wood2018](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_00050314 "Open lateral accessory lobe on L3 CNS template, Wood2018 in Virtual Fly Brain") include PFL1, PFL2_PB4, PFL3_PB7, PFL1_PB1, PFL1_PB7, and PFL1_PB2, as recorded in VFB. Additionally, VFB records show that larval mushroom body output neurons, such as c2, f2, and m1, and larval dopaminergic neurons, like DM1b, also connect the central complex to the lateral accessory lobe. 

VFB holds numerous records of neurons with some part in, or synaptic terminals in, both the adult central complex and the lateral accessory lobe on L3 CNS template, Wood2018. For example, VFB has annotated [363](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003632,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in adult central complex") neurons with some part in adult central complex and [8](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=VFB_00050314,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in embryonic/larval lateral accessory lobe") neurons with some part in embryonic/larval lateral accessory lobe. 

The strength of these connections is not specified in the available evidence. To further investigate the connectivity between the adult central complex and the lateral accessory lobe on L3 CNS template, Wood2018, you can explore the available images of neurons with some part in these brain regions, which include [1404](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=VFB_00050314,ImagesNeurons "Run in VFB: Images of neurons with some part in embryonic/larval lateral accessory lobe") images for the lateral accessory lobe and [13781](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003632,ImagesNeurons "Run in VFB: Images of neurons with some part in adult central complex") images for the adult central complex, as well as the parts of the adult central complex and tracts/nerves innervating both regions that VFB has annotated.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior, as described by Thomas and Wyman (1984). VFB records show that the giant fiber neuron has a distinct anatomy and connectivity. 

VFB holds [22](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") records of images of the giant fiber neuron, which can be used to study its anatomy. Additionally, VFB has annotated [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") records of transgene expression in the giant fiber neuron, which can provide information on its expression pattern and associated GAL4 drivers. 

The connectome data indicates that the giant fiber neuron has downstream connectivity classes ([361](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records) and upstream connectivity classes ([435](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records), which can be used to study its connectivity. 

For more information on the giant fiber neuron, you can explore the available images, transgene expression data, and connectivity classes in VFB. Relevant publications, such as the one by Thomas and Wyman (1984), can also provide more insights into the giant fiber neuron's anatomy, connectivity, and function.

results.title: Hypothesis generation
results.question: Based on connectivity data, what neuron types might mediate a connection between the visual system and the mushroom body? Could visual information reach the memory circuit?
results.response:
Based on connectivity data, several neuron types might mediate a connection between the [visual system](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047735 "Open visual system in Virtual Fly Brain") and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain"). According to VFB, neurons such as [CB2311](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20005873 "Open CB2311 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [CB2443](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20005995 "Open CB2443 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [CB3379](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20006842 "Open CB3379 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [MB-C2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100228 "Open MB-C2 in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [MB-M1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100229 "Open MB-M1 in Virtual Fly Brain"), which have some part in the mushroom body, could be involved in this connection. Additionally, VFB records show that neurons like [ML-VPN2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052139 "Open ML-VPN2 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Mt-VPN1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052141 "Open Mt-VPN1 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Mt-VPN](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052140 "Open Mt-VPN in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Mti](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052142 "Open Mti in Virtual Fly Brain"), and T4ai, which have some part in the visual system, might also play a role. Furthermore, VFB data indicates that adult visual projection neurons, which have presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body, could mediate the connection between the visual system and the mushroom body, as suggested by Vogt et al., 2016. 

VFB holds a substantial amount of data on both the visual system and the mushroom body, including records of neurons with synaptic terminals, presynaptic terminals, and postsynaptic terminals in these systems. For the visual system, VFB has annotated [1046](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047735,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in visual system") neurons with some part in the visual system, while for the mushroom body, VFB has annotated [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") neurons with some part in the mushroom body. This data suggests that visual information could potentially reach the memory circuit via these neuron types. To further explore the connectivity between the visual system and the mushroom body, one could investigate the specific neuron types and their synaptic connections in more detail using VFB's data.

results.title: Novel circuit exploration
results.question: What is the connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the mushroom body? Could temperature information influence memory formation?
results.response:
The connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") can be explored through the available data in VFB. VFB holds downstream connectivity classes for [thermosensory neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005918 "Open thermosensory neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") ([430](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005918,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for thermosensory neuron") records) and upstream connectivity classes for thermosensory neuron ([263](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005918,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for thermosensory neuron") records), which may indicate potential connections to higher brain centers, including the mushroom body. Additionally, VFB records show that thermosensory projection neurons relay temperature-detecting neurons to higher brain centers. 

VFB also holds extensive data on the mushroom body, including neurons with some part in mushroom body ([602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") records), neurons with synaptic terminals in mushroom body ([599](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsSynaptic "Run in VFB: Neurons with synaptic terminals in mushroom body") records), and neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body ([367](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body") records). These data suggest that the mushroom body is a complex structure with many neuronal connections.

Given the role of thermosensory neurons in detecting temperature and the potential connectivity to the mushroom body, it is possible that temperature information could influence memory formation, as the mushroom body is known to be involved in learning and memory. However, the exact nature of this connectivity and its influence on memory formation would require a narrower follow-up. 

Follow-up queries could explore the specific connections between thermosensory neurons and the mushroom body, or investigate the expression patterns overlapping mushroom body ([23](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,ExpressionOverlapsHere "Run in VFB: Expression patterns overlapping mushroom body") records) to gain further insight into the potential relationship between temperature information and memory formation.
